Anya: heads-up — after switching the reranker to int8 PTQ for the small model, synthetic eval (auto-gen queries) shows MRR +0.5% and NDCG roughly flat, but the human-annotated holdout is down ~1.8% MRR. seems weird, any ideas? :thinking:
Sanjay: do we have the exact eval commands for both runs? could be dataset/candidate differences rather than quantization per se.
Anya: yes, here are the commands we ran:
```
# fp16 baseline
python eval/rerank_eval.py --model /models/rerank-v2-fp16 --candidates candidates/bm25_top100.json --labels data/human_holdout.json --metrics ndcg,mrr

# int8 ptq
python eval/rerank_eval.py --model /models/rerank-v2-int8 --candidates candidates/bm25_top100.json --labels data/human_holdout.json --metrics ndcg,mrr
```
Both used the same candidate file. logs: fp16 MRR=0.427, int8 MRR=0.419. synthetic MRR: fp16=0.402 -> int8=0.404.
Mike: a few quick checks: 1) tokenization drift (different tokenizer binaries linked in quant build), 2) nondeterministic KV cache ordering / tie-breakers, 3) deduping / candidate normalization differences.
Eva: + also check if the human set has lots of near-ties. Quant noise can flip ranks when scores are very close. compute per-query score spreads.
Anya: good point — I computed per-query winner margin histogram, and human set has a big spike of very small margins (<0.002) compared to synthetic. might explain flips.
Sanjay: can we run a "swap test" (pairwise sign change counts) between fp16 and int8 to see how many pairwise orderings changed? that often correlates with MRR drops.
Anya: running that now. quick snippet I use to compute pairwise flips:
```
# pseudo
for q in queries:
  for i,j in pairs(candidates[q]):
    flips += sign(score_fp16[q,i]-score_fp16[q,j]) != sign(score_int8[q,i]-score_int8[q,j])
```
I'll push results in a bit.
ci-bot: nightly-eval job 2024-11-02T08:12:00 completed (artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/1725008765/).
Mike: also check label granularity — if human labels are coarse (relevant vs not) then small score shifts matter more for MRR than ndcg depending on cutoff.
Eva: if swaps correlate with low-text-sim queries (code snippets, punctuation-heavy), tokenizer differences could magnify quant perturbations. filter queries by char-type and recompute.
Anya: swap test done: ~12% pairwise order flips on human set vs ~3% on synthetic. flips concentrated in top-10 and where fp16 top score minus runner-up < 0.003.
Sanjay: that's consistent. action plan: 1) verify tokenizers identical (binary sha), 2) add small stable tie-breaking (e.g., deterministic doc-id tiebreak), 3) try bias-correction: add small calibrated offset learned on a small dev set, 4) run per-query delta waterfall to prioritize queries causing most MRR loss.
Mike: for (3) we can fit a cheap isotonic/logistic calibration on int8 scores to align to fp16 rank ordering on dev set. might reduce flips.
Eva: sounds good. i'd also like to run int8 with per-layer rounding check (if PTQ tool supports) and watch which layers contribute largest L2 change. could help narrow root cause.
Anya: thanks. i'll: 1) checksum tokenizers, 2) compute per-layer L2 diffs from ptq tool, 3) implement deterministic tie-break, 4) try small score calibration and report back.
Sanjay: if calibration fixes it, we should add it as a standard post-quant step for rerankers.
Anya: noted. will post results in this thread later. :+1:
